title: LLY, ABBV Stocks Hit All-Time High – Here’s What’s Driving Investor Enthusiasm Today - Asianet Newsable
content: Shares of Eli Lilly (LLY) and AbbVie (ABBV) climbed to new record highs on Friday after the pharmaceutical behemoths reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised their full-year 2026 outlooks. LLY stock was up 3.5% at the time of writing, extending its gains to a fifth straight session. It is on track to post its biggest monthly gains since November 2025. Meanwhile, ABBV shares rose 1.6%. Analysts turned bullish on Eli Lilly (LLY) on Friday, betting on its obesity-drug leadership and expanding pipeline. Scotiabank raised its target to $1,605 from $1,300 and held an ‘Outperform’ rating, expecting Lilly to maintain its obesity-market dominance through ‘next-generation products’ and acquisitions. Truist lifted its target to $1,612 from $1,376, and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating. The firm said Lilly currently has only about 10% market penetration in obesity, and expansion of its incretin franchise and pipeline will cement its dominance in “diabesity” for years to come. On Thursday, Lilly reported a 39% increase in Q3 revenue to $24.4 billion, while adjusted earnings rose 7% to $7.48 per share. Mounjaro sales surged 65% to $10.72 billion, while Zepbound revenue rose 49% to $5.35 billion. Lilly also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $91 billion-$92 billion from $85 billion-$87 billion. However, the company trimmed its bottom-line guidance to $35-$36 per share from $35.5-$36.5 per share. UBS said Lilly’s underlying momentum and a higher Q4 growth run rate could potentially make current estimates appear too conservative. Retail sentiment surrounding LLY on Stocktwits turned ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ a day earlier. The stock has gained more than 31% so far in 2026. AbbVie reported better-than-expected Q3 earnings on Friday, driven by strong growth in its immunology business. Revenue rose 10.3% to $17.40 billion, beating Wall Street’s estimates of $17.34 billion, according to Fiscal.ai. Adjusted earnings more than doubled to $3.82 per share, exceeding consensus estimates of $3.77 per share. Immunology revenue increased 16.3%, with Skyrizi, its autoimmune drug for psoriatic arthritis and Crohn’s disease, among others, generating $5.78 billion. Rinvoq, prescribed for inflammatory conditions including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema, saw sales surge nearly 24%. AbbVie also raised its FY 2026 revenue forecast to $67.8 billion from $67.6 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95 - $13.99 from $13.76 - $13.96. In a call with analysts, chief scientific officer Roopal Thakkar said the company is interested in expanding its obesity-treatment pipeline, according to The Fly. Meanwhile, retail sentiment for ABBV on Stocktwits remained ‘neutral’ over the past 24 hours. The stock has gained about 29% in 2026. title: What AbbVie (ABBV) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call - TradingView
content: AbbVie ABBV reported third-quarter 2026 results above its guidance midpoint and raised its full-year revenue and adjusted earnings outlook, citing continued growth from its immunology and neuroscience portfolios. The company posted adjusted earnings per share of $3.82, $0.07 above the midpoint of its prior guidance. Net revenue totaled $17.4 billion, up 10.5% operationally, excluding foreign exchange, and exceeded AbbVie’s expectations by $200 million, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Rob Michael said on the company’s earnings call. AbbVie raised its 2026 revenue forecast by $200 million to approximately $67.8 billion and lifted adjusted EPS guidance by $0.11 at the midpoint to a range of $13.95 to $13.99. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $18.4 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.83 to $3.87. AbbVie also announced a 5.2% increase in its quarterly cash dividend to $1.82 per share, beginning with the dividend payable in February 2027. Immunology revenue approached $9.2 billion during the quarter, representing 16.6% operational growth. SKYRIZI generated nearly $5.8 billion in sales, up 22.9% operationally, while RINVOQ sales rose 24.3% operationally to $2.7 billion. Michael said SKYRIZI and RINVOQ together are expected to deliver approximately $6 billion in combined growth during 2026 despite increased competition. AbbVie raised its full-year immunology sales forecast to $34.9 billion, including $21.8 billion for SKYRIZI and $10.3 billion for RINVOQ. SKYRIZI received U.S. approval for subcutaneous induction treatment in Crohn’s disease, a new dosing option based on the Phase III AFFIRM study. Chief Scientific Officer Roopal Thakkar said results in patients who had not previously received advanced therapy included a 60% endoscopic response rate, 43% endoscopic remission rate and 74% clinical remission rate after 16 weeks. Chief Commercial Officer Jeff Stewart said the new administration option should strengthen SKYRIZI’s competitive position in Crohn’s disease. He said AbbVie expects access to ramp over roughly 60 days or longer and anticipates faster share gains during the first part of 2027 and into the second quarter. AbbVie is also evaluating combinations of SKYRIZI with ABBV-382, an anti-alpha-4 beta-7 antibody, and ABBV-701, an anti-TL1A antibody, in Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Thakkar said the company could potentially begin Phase III testing of the ABBV-382 combination by the end of 2027, depending on interim data and dose-selection work. Humira sales were $683 million, declining 30.6% operationally as biosimilar competition continued. Neuroscience revenue was nearly $3.4 billion, up 19.5% operationally. AbbVie increased its full-year neuroscience revenue outlook by $300 million to $13 billion, including expected sales of $4.2 billion each for VRAYLAR and BOTOX Therapeutic, as well as $3.1 billion in oral CGRP migraine treatments. VRAYLAR sales reached nearly $1.1 billion, up 14.3% operationally. BOTOX Therapeutic generated about $1.1 billion, up 9.8%, while UBRELVY revenue increased 26.9% to $449 million and Qulipta revenue climbed more than 38% to $398 million. The FDA approved JUVMO for Parkinson’s disease during the quarter. AbbVie said the treatment selectively targets D1/D5 dopamine receptors and can be used as either monotherapy or alongside standard care. The company expects its Parkinson’s disease therapies, including JUVMO, VYALEV and DUOPA, to eventually generate more than $5 billion in peak sales collectively. Stewart said JUVMO’s sales ramp is expected to be gradual because broader Medicare coverage is not expected until 2028. Still, he said early physician and patient interest has exceeded AbbVie’s initial expectations. Oncology revenue totaled $1.7 billion, up 0.9% operationally. VENCLEXTA sales rose 10.7% to $803 million, while IMBRUVICA sales declined 26.1% due to Inflation Reduction Act pricing and competitive pressure. AbbVie raised its full-year oncology forecast to $6.6 billion, now expecting $3.1 billion in VENCLEXTA revenue and $2.1 billion from IMBRUVICA. The company recently submitted a U.S. regulatory application for etentamig in heavily pretreated, triple-class exposed multiple myeloma following positive Phase III CERVINO data. Thakkar said the company expects an approval decision next year. AbbVie also started two additional Phase III studies for etentamig, including a combination study in second-line-plus multiple myeloma and a monotherapy study in light-chain amyloidosis. In lymphoma, AbbVie reported positive Phase III data for Epkinly plus R-CHOP in first-line diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The regimen reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 51% versus R-CHOP alone at an interim analysis, according to Thakkar. Regulatory submissions are expected early next year. AbbVie generated approximately $14 billion in free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026 and ended September with $10.8 billion in cash. The company said it remains on track to reduce its net leverage ratio to 2x over the next two to three years following its Apogee Therapeutics acquisition. Michael said future business-development activity is likely to focus on bolt-on additions in immunology, neuroscience, oncology and obesity rather than a large transformational transaction. Aesthetics sales were nearly $1.2 billion, down 1.8% operationally. BOTOX Cosmetic sales rose 4.1% operationally to $669 million, while JUVÉDERM sales fell 11.8% to $222 million. AbbVie maintained its full-year aesthetics outlook of $5 billion. Regarding Boey, the company said it expects to resubmit its U.S. application before year-end after addressing chemistry, manufacturing and controls matters cited in a complete response letter. Thakkar said AbbVie anticipates a six-month review and a potential U.S. decision in mid-2027. Michael also said a federal district court ruled in AbbVie’s favor on whether BOTOX should be eligible for Medicare drug-price negotiation under the Inflation Reduction Act. The ruling may be appealed by the government, and AbbVie said it would not expect a negotiated price to be published while the matter remains unresolved. AbbVie Inc ABBV is a global biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops and commercializes medicines and other healthcare products. Its portfolio focuses on immunology, oncology, neuroscience, aesthetics and eye care, serving patients and healthcare providers in markets around the world. The company's key products include immunology medicines such as Skyrizi and Rinvoq; neuroscience treatments including Vraylar, Ubrelvy and Qulipta; and oncology products such as Imbruvica and Venclexta. ABBV reported adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.82 for the third quarter of 2026, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.74. The reported metric even surpassed management's guidance of $3.73-$3.77. Earnings surged 105.4% year over year, with the prior-year period burdened by a substantially larger acquired research and development (R&D) charge. Revenues of $17.4 billion topped the consensus mark of $17.37 billion, rising 10.3% year over year on a reported basis and 10.5% at constant exchange rates (CER). Neuroscience revenues grew 19.5% to $3.39 billion, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.29 billion. Vraylar contributed $1.07 billion, up 14.3%, although sales fell short of the $1.08 billion consensus estimate. Botox Therapeutic revenues advanced 9.8% to $1.08 billion. "We also enhanced our long-term growth potential by securing key regulatory approvals, generating differentiated clinical data and completing the acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics. Given our strong outlook and significant momentum, we are once again increasing AbbVie's full-year guidance and raising our quarterly dividend." A company’s long-term revenue performance is one signal of its overall quality. Any business can deliver a good quarter or two, but the best consistently grow over the long term. Over the last five years, AbbVie grew its revenue at a tepid 3.7% compounded annual growth rate, an underwhelming result compared with the rest of the healthcare sector. Still, there are things to like about AbbVie. This quarter, AbbVie’s year-on-year revenue growth was 10.3%, and its $17.4 billion of revenue was in line with Wall Street’s consensus estimates. Looking ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 8.8% over the next 12 months, according to S&P, similar to its two-year rate. This projection is particularly noteworthy for a company of its scale and suggests the market expects success for its products and services. Adjusted operating margin is a key measure of profitability. Think of it as net income (the bottom line) excluding the impact of non-recurring expenses, taxes and interest on debt – metrics less connected to business fundamentals. AbbVie has performed well over the last five years. It demonstrated high profitability for a healthcare business, with an average adjusted operating margin of 44%. Looking at the trend in its profitability, AbbVie’s adjusted operating margin decreased by 9.7 percentage points over the last five years. The company’s two-year trajectory also shows it failed to restore profitability to its peak as its margin fell by 3 percentage points. This was a poor performance, indicating its expenses were rising and it couldn’t pass those costs on to its customers. This quarter, AbbVie generated an adjusted operating margin of 36%, up 5.1 percentage points year on year. This increase was a positive development and shows it was more efficient. We track the long-term change in earnings per share (EPS) for the same reason as long-term revenue growth. Compared to revenue, however, EPS highlights whether a company’s growth is profitable. AbbVie’s flat EPS over the last five years was below its 3.7% annualized revenue growth. This tells us the company became less profitable on a per-share basis as it expanded. A closer look at AbbVie’s earnings helps explain the drivers of its performance. As noted earlier, AbbVie’s adjusted operating margin expanded this quarter but declined by 9.7 percentage points over the last five years. This was the most relevant factor (aside from the revenue impact) behind its lower earnings; interest expenses and taxes can also affect EPS but don’t tell us as much about a company’s fundamentals. In Q3, AbbVie reported adjusted EPS of $3.82, up from $1.86 in the same quarter last year. This result beat analysts’ consensus estimates by 1.3%. Over the next 12 months, Wall Street expects AbbVie’s full-year EPS to grow 21.2% from $12.83 to $15.54, according to S&P. AbbVie delivered a solid third quarter including a raise in adjusted EPS guidance. Shares remained flat at $289.68 immediately after the report. Pharmaceutical company AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV) will be reporting earnings tomorrow before market open. Here's what to expect. AbbVie beat analysts' revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $16.99 billion, up 10.2% year on year. It was a mixed quarter for the company, with a narrow beat of analysts' EPS estimates but a slight miss of analysts' full-year EPS guidance estimates. Is AbbVie a buy or sell going into earnings? Read our full analysis here, it's free for active Edge members. This quarter, the market is expecting AbbVie's revenue to grow 9.9% year on year, in line with the 9.1% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year. Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. AbbVie has a history of exceeding Wall Street's expectations. Looking at AbbVie's peers in the biotechnology segment, only Biogen has reported results so far. It exceeded analysts' revenue estimates, delivering year-on-year sales growth of 10.6%. Read our full analysis of Biogen's earnings results here. There has been positive sentiment among investors in the biotechnology segment, with share prices up 6.1% on average over the last month. AbbVie is up 10.6% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $283.19 (compared to the current share price of $289.23).
